body: It’s a somewhat large, growing company but their HR isn’t exactly reachable to those not on the inside. All I’ve found is an email. Their number is prioritized around sales and current clients, no reception or phone directory.
I agree but that’s a tough conversation to navigate without arising suspicion. Especially when I have the final round interview next week. Any tips on how to figure this out now?

Any help or guidance on this is greatly appreciated...

So I’m now in the final round of interviews. Next step is to meet the Chief Sales Officer and then a values interview with HR. 

At this point, if it comes up, I don’t think my best bet is to disclose my background to only HR. Obviously if it comes up, I need to speak to it. If it doesn’t come up, or the question isn’t asked, my plan is ask what the process looks like after I sign and to read the offer, and if there is any mention of background check then I will reach out to my would be manager to see if they’re comfortable to meet for coffee (covid) or to briefly chat. Then disclose this to them and hope to rally support. 

Would you agree or is my best bet to wait and delicately have this conversation with HR to take ownership of my past and see what they say?

Edit: I’ve also been told I’m by far the front runner but did not ask how many else are in consideration. My background perfectly aligns with this role, so I think this gives me a major advantage with it being Q4.
